extracted.intended_audience: general readers, journalists, researchers and policy audiences interested in EU external action and disinformation
extracted.subtask_short: encyclopedic overview of EU StratCom unit
extracted.subtask_description: A Wikipedia-style, neutral encyclopedia article describing the East StratCom Task Force: its history, mission, products, reception, criticisms, and factual record. The page summarizes organizational aims, activities (EUvsDisinfo), and public reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective communication and promotion of EU activities
rubrics_metrics.description: The East StratCom Task Force is focused on "effective communication" and promotion of European Union activities in Eastern Europe (including Armenia, Azerbaijan, Belarus, Georgia, Moldova, and Ukraine) and beyond (Russia).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Products are intended for the EU's political leadership, press services, EU delegations and EU member states and are intended for the general public. The group's remit is to communicate about issues where EU strategic communication needs to be improved, or the EU is subject to disinformation campaigns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flagship project: EUvsDisinfo database
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain and publish EUvsDisinfo — a database of articles, media, and analysis of Foreign Information Manipulation and Interference (FIMI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The full record of the Task Force's work on disinformation is available on EUvsDisinfo.eu in multiple languages; the database is the team's main tool to document and analyse disinformation cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop targeted communication campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop communication campaigns targeting key audiences and focused on specific issues of relevance to those audiences, including local issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Actions should be built on existing work and coherent with wider EU communication efforts, including activities of the EU institutions and EU member states; campaigns can be coordinated with the European Commission (example: Eastern Partnership communications campaign).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use local languages and appropriate dissemination channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce communications mainly focused on the countries of the Eastern Neighbourhood and produced in the local languages of those countries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disseminate via social media channels of the EU Delegations in the region, television, other media and public events to maximise local reach and relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide regular, analyst-focused outputs (Disinformation Review)
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce a weekly Disinformation Review (in English and Russian) to provide data for analysts, journalists and officials dealing with disinformation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Review brings the latest news and analyses of what the Task Force labels as "pro-Kremlin disinformation" and is intended to raise awareness and serve as a resource for professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish disinformation from legitimate dissent
rubrics_metrics.description: A core challenge is to correctly distinguish disinformation from legitimate dissent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requires careful sourcing, balanced judgement and attention to democratic norms; failure to distinguish can generate criticism about censorship or bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain multilingual, publicly accessible records and social presence
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the Task Force's work accessible on its website and run EEAS language services and social accounts (Twitter, Facebook) to communicate EU foreign policy and Task Force outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability in multiple languages (English, Russian, German, etc.) and active social media presence broaden reach and support transparency; Twitter reach metrics (e.g., up to 2 million people/month) are cited as outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Focus subject-matter effort where threat is greatest
rubrics_metrics.description: Concentrate most efforts on providing information support on issues related to the Russo‑Ukrainian War.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizational priorities should reflect the salience of disinformation campaigns; historic counts (cases related to COVID-19 and the war in Ukraine) illustrate topical focus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy in identification and classification of disinformation
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure correctness when including items in the disinformation database (avoid incorrect inclusion due to translation errors or misclassification).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Past mistakes (e.g., incorrectly including three Dutch articles due partly to a translation error) led to legal action and required removal of items and changes to the language used when describing outlets; this implies procedures for verification and review are necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use careful, legally-aware language about accused outlets
rubrics_metrics.description: When identifying outlets as publishing disinformation, use cautious, non-defamatory language and have clear justification for claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ESTF's removal of cases and changes in wording after lawsuits illustrates the need for conservative phrasing, documentation of evidence and legal-risk awareness to avoid libel suits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide fact-based background information to improve representation of EU policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer fact-based background information about the Union to increase visibility and more accurate representation of EU policies in regionally relevant languages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As noted by officials, providing accurate, fact-based content in local languages helps counter misleading narratives and supports journalists and audiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate with EU institutions and member states
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure actions are coherent with wider EU communication efforts and coordinate with EU institutions, the European Commission, and member states.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordination allows scaling (e.g., 'StratCom Plus' preparatory actions) and leverages resources across institutions for campaigns like the Eastern Partnership communications drive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate staffing and resourcing
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintain sufficient staffing and resources to meet mission objectives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Critics and EU Parliament appeals have emphasised the need for adequate staffing and funding; initial reliance on donations and small staff constrained capacity until EU budget funding began in 2018.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure and report output and impact metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Collect and report metrics such as number of disinformation cases identified, topical breakdowns, weekly averages and social reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples in the article: 1,992 confirmed cases (2015–16), more than 6,000 cases (2015–2019), counts for COVID-19 and the war in Ukraine, and social media reach figures—these serve as transparency and impact indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be prepared to correct errors and adapt processes
rubrics_metrics.description: When errors are identified (e.g., wrongful inclusion of articles), promptly remove or correct records and adapt language or processes to prevent repeats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ESTF removed disputed articles, changed its descriptive language, and engaged with critics — illustrating corrective actions and process adaptation as part of quality control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Serve as an early-warning and monitoring capability
rubrics_metrics.description: Act as an early warning system to detect incoming Kremlin or other foreign disinformation campaigns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Media descriptions portray the Task Force as a frontline capability; this implies continuous monitoring, rapid reporting, and readiness to brief decision-makers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Produce concise, shareable assets (tweets, infographics) for policymakers
rubrics_metrics.description: Create short, shareable communications (daily tweets, infographics) and briefings aimed at MEPs and senior EU officials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observers recommended that the Disinformation Review, daily tweets and infographics should be readily available to MEPs and senior officials to inform policy and public messaging.
